key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes bandgap and photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best solar absorber.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies composition control as a practical route to optimize perovskite solar cell efficiency and select materials for optoelectronic device design.
method: Electronic band structure and optical parameter analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV across the series and a peak SLME efficiency of 29.6% for Ca3PI3, versus 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: These results are computational and screening-based, so experimental stability, synthesis feasibility, and device-level losses still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
